blindComparison: No blind comparison was performed. No reference media was used and the reviewer knew this product's identity. E-13 remains not measured; these source and CPU failures do not produce a blind/reference verdict.

dependenciesForCorrection.reason: Authored prop id must identify the actual emission source before shutVents or halfVents can affect it.

Reset addresses prop IDs, save emits only truthy source IDs, and load applies those rows. Old saves contain decision flags but omit the three null-ID sources, so an ID-only code fix cannot by itself restore an old decision.
Source rebakes, wind advection and intensity smoothing change samples over time; planned route costs must follow within a bounded update interval.
Cost-aware node search, segment smoothing, direct steering and cached routes must agree; fixing only the initial cost calculation leaves two bypasses.

findings.fix: Use consistent source IDs across authored props, hooks, reset and save/load. Run node ../gas-vent-id-probe.mjs and require all 3 authored source IDs to be present and inactive after the real shutVents hook. Reconcile existing shut/half decisions when older saves omit those source rows.
findings.hypothesis: Confirmed mechanism: world_data supplies p.id; City._prop passes p.gasId || null to GasField.addSource. The hook and reset address p.id. Save filters out null source IDs, so old saves omit these three sources.
findings.problem: The three West Heads gas sources are registered with id:null. The actual shutVents hook returns false for all three deactivation requests, leaves all three emitting, and activates yard_seep instead.
findings.refutation: Independent full City / Director hook / in-memory save and restore checks also returned false for the three deactivations, saved zero West Heads rows, and restored a vents_shut save with those sources still active. Atmospheric methods were stubs: their call intent was measured, not their visible output.
findings.shot: actual City / shutVents hook / paired Game.fixedUpdate
findings.why: The closing choice has no gas-reduction benefit at the three heads, while the receiving yard becomes dangerous.

independentIntensityControl.scope: Independent actual full City CPU build; only GasField.setIntensity(2) then 120 updates of 0.5s, no Game actor or narrative execution. Source search establishes runtime Game uses gas.update and has no navigation refresh caller.

evidence.note: The manual refresh is a diagnostic counterfactual; it is not performed by the actual update path.

findings.fix: Refresh or invalidate gas traversal costs after meaningful field changes within a bounded update interval. Run node ../gas-consequence-probe.mjs and compare the live stored costs with the current field, rather than relying on an initialization-only map.
findings.hypothesis: Confirmed source mechanism: City.build is the only applyGasCost caller. Game.fixedUpdate updates GasField without updating NavGrid; GasField source/intensity/wind updates do not notify it.
findings.problem: After the actual vent hook and one second of Game.fixedUpdate, the entire navigation cost buffer remains byte-identical although 1,850 walkable cells have gas increases above 1 ppm. A diagnostic refresh changes 36,462 stored costs.
findings.refutation: An independent actual City intensity/wind control also retains the initial cost hash despite 31,156 changed expected costs. This proves stale planner costs, not absence of every reactive enemy movement.
findings.shot: actual City / live source change and 60 Game.fixedUpdate steps
findings.why: The route planner continues to use the initial gas snapshot after source, wind or intensity changes.

findings.fix: Keep hazard cost meaningful during smoothing. Reproduce the 13x9 setup in gas-consequence-refutation.json with node ../gas-navigation-probe.mjs; require returned segments to retain the lower-exposure detour instead of the central cost-6.5 shortcut.
findings.hypothesis: Confirmed source and independent CPU mechanism: NavGrid._clear checks walkability, bounds and height, but not traversal cost.
findings.problem: A* predecessors detour around a plume with route-cell costs below 1.38, but findPath returns only start and target, yielding a straight segment through the central cost-6.5 cell.
findings.refutation: Survived independent reproduction with a freshly computed gas cost map. The fixture uses a constructed flat floor, not a claimed travelled route through the shipped City.
findings.shot: CPU 13x9 open floor / real NavGrid and GasField
findings.why: Updating the cost buffer alone does not preserve the safe route; string pulling removes its hazard-avoiding waypoints.

evidence.scope: Real _moveTowards with a stored detour, actual collision world, gas and NavGrid; desired movement is measured, not an integrated travelled trajectory.

findings.fix: Account for gas exposure in the direct-steering decision or preserve a safer current detour. Run node ../gas-navigation-probe.mjs with the recorded 4m target and require the unsafe shortcut not to erase that detour.
findings.hypothesis: Confirmed source and CPU mechanism: d<6 plus collision line-of-sight enters a direct-steering branch that does not read GasField or NavGrid cost.
findings.problem: At a clear four-metre hop, _moveTowards discards a stored detour, makes zero pathfinder calls, and requests straight movement across a plume whose centre is about 2,260 ppm.
findings.refutation: Survived as a requested-movement defect. It does not prove that the enemy completes the crossing before later gas panic can redirect it.
findings.shot: CPU 4m AI movement request / real collision, NavGrid and GasField
findings.why: The normal short-hop branch bypasses gas-aware planning even if costs and smoothing are corrected.

independentRefuter.state: Completed. All four concrete findings survived independent source/CPU refutation; the claim of no reactive gas-driven enemy movement was refuted.

limits: No product files, browser, server or remote state were changed or launched by this reviewer.
The City fixture stubs Canvas drawing, text metrics and material appearance. Geometry, collision, navigation and gas are actual code.
Atmosphere fog values were tested with inert particle/light-pool updates; no image or GPU result was measured.
The reproduction hooks bypass user interaction deliberately. They test the actual consequence functions, not touch controls, dialogue usability or acquisition of rigVent.
All raw baseline evidence is pinned to d19c424. Subsequent fixes are outside this report until separately verified.
E-13 remains not measured because no valid blind comparison has occurred.

reactiveCounterexample.claim: Gas has no effect on enemy routes or behaviour at all.
reactiveCounterexample.scope: Uses real Enemy perception/localPpm/Actor.setMove/AISystem._updateEnemy/_flee methods, real GasField and Lungs, with constructor state set in memory and no renderer or physics integration. Clear air stays idle; high air emits gaspanic, enters FLEE and requests movement down the sampled gradient. This establishes existing reactive steering, not reliable obstacle-free escape or global cost-optimal movement.

survival.conclusion: For a stationary, unmasked scav at the affected yard point, the control remains at 62 HP for 600 seconds; the treated field causes death at 87.7 seconds.
survival.limit: Actual Enemy construction and Actor._updateVitals/Lungs were used with the field frozen after one second. This is fixed exposure, not a playthrough or an enemy allowed to flee. It is a game simulation result, not a physiological claim.
